title: Pre-Analysis Round 2 — Freighter Hard Point Provisioning Extended to the Later Build Standard
abstract: Second round of pre-analysis on the freighter hard point provisioning, asking what the later cargo compartment fit does to the restraint grid now that conversion demand has moved to aircraft delivered after the original effectivity closed.

sections.objective: Re-examine the main deck hard point provisioning for aircraft outside the original effectivity, after three conversion enquiries arrived for airframes delivered later than the range the first round covered. The round had to establish what the brushless cargo loading fit and the extended discharge suppression standard do to the restraint grid and to the floor panel edge condition, and whether the post-mod protection condition set in the first round still holds on the later build.
sections.findings_summary: Two of the three items are conditions rather than obstacles. The brushless drive unit and roller tray upgrade occupies the same compartment volume and shares the two lower deck zones; its short-pitch tray spacing does not align with the original hard point pitch, so a converted aircraft carrying the upgrade needs a transition tray that nobody has drawn. The extended discharge suppression standard rebalanced the distribution manifold across the same compartment and its nozzle coverage was substantiated for a passenger lining that a conversion removes. The floor panel edge elongation repair is the third item and is the cleanest: aircraft with an elongated insert repair at a hard point station cannot take the fitting without a local renewal, which changes the conversion downtime estimate materially.
sections.next_steps: Draw the transition tray and get the cargo loading owner to accept it as part of the provisioning scope rather than the conversion scope. Ask fire protection for a written position on nozzle coverage with the lining removed, and treat it as a condition of the effectivity extension rather than a separate study. Add a pre-conversion insert repair survey to the provisioning instructions and revise the downtime estimate. Carry the protection standard condition forward unchanged.

similarity_seeds: hard point provisioning so a later conversion does not open the floor grid
restraint fitting pitch on a main deck cargo floor

tasks.title: Re-run the compartment search against the later build standard
Compare restraint grid pitch with the installed loading system
Obtain a suppression coverage position for the converted lining
Quantify the repair population at hard point stations

expected_findings.rationale: The upgraded loading system uses a short-pitch roller tray whose spacing does not align with the hard point stations set by the provisioning. On an aircraft carrying both, a conversion cannot lay the restraint grid without lifting and re-spacing trays that were never designed to move.
expected_findings.resolution: Draw a transition tray and add it to the provisioning scope with its own part list.

evidence.similarity_note: Entity linked through the two lower deck compartment zones and the shared secondary chapter. The two texts have almost nothing in common: one is a floor structure document, the other a suppression distribution document.

expected_findings.rationale: The extended discharge standard rebalanced the distribution manifold and substantiated nozzle coverage against a passenger compartment lining. A converted aircraft removes that lining, which changes the free volume and the flow path the substantiation assumed.
expected_findings.resolution: Obtain a written coverage position and make it a condition of the effectivity extension.

evidence.similarity_note: Both entity linking and similarity returned it; the repair and the provisioning describe the same panel edge and insert population in the same words.

expected_findings.rationale: An elongated insert repair at a hard point station leaves no sound material for the fitting. The provisioning instructions assume a pristine edge condition, and the repair population at those stations is not negligible on the later build.
expected_findings.resolution: Add a pre-conversion insert repair survey and revise the downtime estimate accordingly.

expected_non_findings.reason: Shares the seat track FIN position and the ATA 53-50 floor structure context, and its title reads like a floor interface change. It works the passenger cabin seat track above the main deck, imposes nothing on the lower deck restraint grid and is scoped to high-density layouts that no conversion candidate carries.

type_data.conclusion: The effectivity extension is sound subject to three conditions: a transition tray, a suppression coverage position and a pre-conversion repair survey. The protection standard condition from round one is carried forward.
